anomalies.observed: Both U1 (INA219AIDCNR) and U2 (PCA9685PW) are connected to the same I2C bus nets I2C2_SCL_FCC and I2C2_SDA_FCC, and both are strapped to I2C address 0x40 (INA219 A0/A1 tied to GND; PCA9685 A0-A5 tied to GND).
anomalies.expected: Two I2C devices on the same bus must have different addresses. The specification lists both the INA219 and PCA9685 with address 0x40, but does not state they are intentionally on separate buses; the schematic shows them on the same I2C2 bus.

evidence.quote: Power sheet: U1 INA219 SDA pin6 label I2C2_SDA_FCC, SCL pin5 I2C2_SCL_FCC; FCC Peripherals sheet: U2 PCA9685 SCL pin26 label I2C2_SCL_FCC, SDA pin27 I2C2_SDA_FCC
Current/voltage sensor | Hades (top sheet) | TI INA219AIDCNR, I2C addr 0x40 ... PWM/servo driver | FCCPeripherals | NXP PCA9685PW (I2C 16-ch PWM), I2C addr 0x40

anomalies.impact: I2C bus contention will occur; neither the current/voltage sensor nor the PWM driver will be reliably addressable.

anomalies.observed: On the Power sheet, REG1 (MIC26903YJL-TR) pin 27 (VIN) and pin 28 (VDD) both connect to the net label REG_VIN.
anomalies.expected: VDD is an internal LDO output on the MIC26903 and should be decoupled to GND with a capacitor; it must not be tied to the input voltage VIN.

evidence.quote: Power sheet: REG1 pin 27 VIN and pin 28 VDD both connect to label REG_VIN
Main buck regulator (5 V rail) | Hades (top sheet) | Microchip MIC26903YJL-TR

anomalies.impact: The internal LDO output is shorted to the battery input, likely preventing the buck regulator from starting or damaging the IC.

anomalies.observed: On the Connections sheet, CH330 U11 pin3 (TXD) connects to UART1_TX_FCC and pin4 (RXD) to UART1_RX_FCC; U12 similarly connects its TXD/RXD straight to UART3_TX_NAVC/UART3_RX_NAVC.
anomalies.expected: A USB-UART bridge's TXD must connect to the MCU's RX line and RXD to the MCU's TX line.

evidence.quote: Connections sheet: U11 pin3 TXD to UART1_TX_FCC, pin4 RXD to UART1_RX_FCC

anomalies.impact: The serial debug/programming interfaces will not communicate because both ends drive the same lines.

parsed.summary: The schematic contains multiple deviations from sound design practice: U1 and U2 share the same I2C address on the same bus, REG1 VDD is tied to VIN instead of being decoupled, and the CH330 UART bridges appear to connect TXD/RXD straight through rather than crossed.
